_note: Stanford university-wide undergraduate requirements -- these apply regardless of major, on top of whatever a person's program sheet(s) require. Compiled from web research on 2026-09-03 without a direct rendered read of the bulletin (org web-fetch was unavailable), cross-checked with a couple of follow-up searches. Anything with a 'confidence' field other than 'verified' should be spot-checked against the linked source before being treated as ground truth by the solver -- surface these to the user rather than silently trusting them.

pass_fail.note: Activity-unit cap sits inside, not on top of, the pass/fail cap. Cap does not include terms officially offered Satisfactory/No Credit only.

wim.note: Writing in the Major -- a third tier, separate from WR1/WR2. Each major designates its own WIM course(s); see that major's program sheet, not this file.

language.requirement_summary: Equivalent of one year of college-level foreign language study (typically 3 quarters), covering oral, reading, and writing skill.

ap_credit_min_score.note: A score of 4 or 5 on the AP foreign-language exam (Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Latin, Spanish) gives credit and satisfies the requirement. AP foreign-*literature* exams do NOT satisfy it.

ways.status: active alongside COLLEGE (not replaced by it)

CE.name: Creative Expression
CE.units_note: 2 units total; may be met with two 1-unit courses in the same department

sequence.title: Why College? Your Education and the Good Life
one of ~8-10 topic options, mostly 4-unit lecture/section, some 3-unit seminar

effective_through_2026_2027.note: Students choose 2 of their first-year's 3 quarters to enroll in COLLEGE.

effective_2027_2028_onward.note: Faculty Senate voted May 2026 to make COLLEGE permanent and extend it from 2 to 3 quarters, effective Fall 2027. If planning schedules for students starting Fall 2027 or later, use 3 quarters, not 2.

overlap_unit_cap.note: No fixed university-wide numeric cap. Overlap between the primary and secondary major is allowed and is worked out case-by-case (via the 'Major-Minor and Multiple Major Course Approval Form', department-approved) -- don't encode a specific number here, treat it as 'ask your department' territory rather than a solver constraint.

double_major.exceptions: Intro-level shared requirements (e.g. intro math/language) and School of Engineering school-wide requirements may still be shared even though double-counting is otherwise disallowed.

degree_type_mixing_ba_bs.value: may mix -- a double major does not require both majors to be the same degree type; one can be BA and the other BS, still resulting in a single diploma

coterm._note: General university policy only. Specific graduate programs (e.g. a CS MS coterm) layer additional requirements on top -- check that program's page separately.
coterm.masters_unit_rules: 100-level or above; at least 50% of units must be primarily graduate-level (typically 200+).
coterm.double_counting_between_degrees: Not generally allowed simultaneously -- the 45 graduate units must be unduplicated relative to the 180 undergraduate units. A separate 'coterm course transfer' mechanism can later re-designate specific units from the undergrad to the grad transcript, which is a reassignment, not simultaneous double-counting.
coterm.overlap_quarter_note: At least one quarter where both the bachelor's and master's programs are simultaneously open on the student's record.
coterm.application_deadline: No later than the quarter before expected bachelor's degree conferral (university floor); individual graduate programs may set earlier deadlines.
coterm.tuition_group_transition: May request to move into the graduate tuition group once 180 units are completed (225 for dual-degree students) or upon bachelor's conferral.
